note: ADDING A FIELD TO PossessOpts IS A REPO-SCOPE EVENT, NOT A WORKSPACE ONE, and cargo clippy --workspace cannot tell you. The Tableau added one optional field and broke TEN full-literal construction sites. Nine were found by a workspace clippy. The tenth, clients/vessel/wasm/src/lib.rs, is in a crate EXCLUDED from the cargo workspace, so --workspace --all-targets never compiled it and every local check was green while the chamber clients phase went red at 1260s. Cost: one full merge slot. THE SEQUENCE THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, and it is cheap: after touching any widely-constructed vessel type, run make vessel-check (builds the wasm ABI crate) and ideally make clients-check-run (all four, and it is the exact thing the chamber runs). Scoping a test run to -p hornvale-vessel hid the CLI pair earlier in the same campaign for the same reason one level in. GENERAL FORM: a struct field is a blast-radius change bounded by the set of crates that CONSTRUCT it, which is not the set the workspace compiles. Two of this repo four client crates are outside the workspace and one of them constructs PossessOpts. Also worth knowing: a grep audit for the remaining sites gave a FALSE ALL-CLEAR because the pattern for the struct-update shorthand did not match the fully-qualified form ..hornvale_vessel::PossessOpts::default(); the fix is to grep for the type name and read each site rather than to pattern-match the escape hatch.
